articles.title: लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफको प्रथम क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
लायन्स इन्टरनेसनल एमडी ३२५ अन्तर्गत डिष्ट्रिक्ट ३२५ एफ, नेपाल (लायन वर्ष २०२६–२०२७) को प्रथम डिष्ट्रिक्ट क्याबिनेट मिटिङ तथा क्याबिनेट अफिसर्स इन्स्टलेसन कार्यक्रम आइतवार सम्पन्न भएको छ । डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नर लायन अजय प्रसाद खनालको अध्यक्षतामा सम्पन्न उक्त क्याबिनेट मिटिङमा डिष्ट्रिक्ट भरिका लायन्स लिडरहरू, क्लब पदाधिकारी तथा सदस्यहरूको उत्साहजनक एवं उल्लेखनीय सहभागिता रहेको थियो । बैठकमा लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको मूल मन्त्र हामी सेवा गर्छौलाई आत्मसात गर्दै चालू लायन वर्षका रणनीतिक योजनाहरू, सेवा गतिविधि, नेतृत्व विकास तथा संगठन सुदृढीकरणका विषयमा गहन र रचनात्मक छलफल गरिएको थियो ।

विशेषगरी, लायन्स इन्टरनेसनलको ग्लोबल कज अन्तर्गतका मुख्य क्षेत्रहरू मधुमेह, दृष्टि, भोक निवारण, पर्यावरण, बाल क्यान्सर, मानवीय कार्य, विपद् राहत र युवा जस्ता विश्वव्यापी प्राथमिकताका कार्यक्रमहरू लगायत डिष्ट्रिक्ट गभर्नरका प्रायोरिटी प्रोजेक्ट तथा मानवीय सेवामूलक अभियानहरूलाई अझ प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढाउने, सदस्यता अभिवृद्धि गर्ने तथा क्लबहरूको सक्रियता र क्षमता विकास बढाउने विषयमा महत्वपूर्ण निर्णयहरू समेत गरिएको छ ।

सोही अवसरमा उपस्थित विशिष्ट नेतृत्वको समुपस्थितिमा नयाँ क्याबिनेट टिमको औपचारिक इन्स्टलेसन (शपथ ग्रहण तथा पदस्थापना) सम्पन्न गरिएको थियो । नवगठित क्याबिनेट टिमले जिम्मेवारी ग्रहण गर्दै आगामी कार्यकालमा समाजमा प्रभावकारी सेवा तथा सबल नेतृत्व प्रदान गर्ने सामूहिक प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेका छन् ।

यस कार्यक्रमलाई भक्तपुर दिबेश्वरी लायन्स क्लबले आतिथ्यता तथा व्यवस्थापकीय सहयोग प्रदान गरेको थियो । उक्त भव्य कार्यक्रमले सम्पूर्ण लायन्स सदस्यहरूमा सेवाभाव, आपसी एकता र समर्पणको भावना अभिवृद्धि गर्दै समाजसेवामा अझ सक्रिय, उर्जावान र प्रभावकारी रूपमा अघि बढ्न ठूलो प्रेरणा दिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: अफवाह होइन सद्भावमा अग्रसरता, सामाजिक–राजनीतिक अगुवा सार्वजनिक आह्वानमा सक्रिय
articles.summary:
सुनसरी । सुनसरीमा दुई समुदायबीच भएको झडपपछि विभिन्न जिल्लामा फैलिएको तनावका बीच कोशी–मधेशका विभिन्न सहरमा सामाजिक सद्भाव र धार्मिक सहिष्णुताको सन्देश दिँदै बृहत् सद्भाव ¥याली आयोजना गरिदैछ । देशका विभिन्न स्थानमा निकालिएका यस्ता ¥यालीले सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम हुने ठानिएको छ ।

सुनसरीमा भएको घटनापछि मधेशका विभिन्न जिल्लामा देखिएको तनावका बीच सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम गर्ने उद्देश्यले बृहत् सद्भाव ¥याली निकालिएको छ । जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय धनुषाको अगुवाइमा आयोजित ¥याली जनकपुरधामस्थित रेल्वे स्टेशनबाट शुरु भइ नगरका विभिन्न मुख्य सडक हुँदै सम्पन्न भएको थियो ।

¥यालीमा राजनीतिक दलका प्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षा निकाय, स्थानीय तहका जनप्रतिनिधि, धार्मिक अगुवा, नागरिक समाज तथा उद्योगी–व्यवसायीहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

धनुषाका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी प्रेमप्रसाद लुइँटेलले मिथिला सभ्यता र संस्कृतिले सधैँ शान्ति, सहिष्णुता र सद्भावको सन्देश दिएको उल्लेख गर्दै सामाजिक एकता जोगाउन सबैलाई जिम्मेवार र संयमित बन्न आग्रह गरे ।

नेपाली कम्युनिष्ट पार्टीका केन्द्रीय सदस्य दीपक यादवले सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न सबै समुदाय एकजुट हुनुपर्ने बताउँदै सुनसरी र सिरहाका घटनाको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गरी दोषीमाथि कारबाही गर्न माग गरे ।

जनकपुरधाम उपमहानगरपालिकाका पूर्वउपमेयर असगर अलीले घटनाबाट प्रभावितलाई न्याय दिलाउनुका साथै समाजमा विश्वास र सद्भाव कायम गर्न समुदायबीच निरन्तर संवाद आवश्यक रहेको बताए ।

यता, मोरङको लेटाङ नगरपालिकाका नगर प्रमुख भुपेन्द्र कुमार लावतीले २०६५ साल देखि नै लेटाङमा अन्तरधार्मिक शान्ति संजाल गठन गरेर सबै धर्म र जातजाति बीच सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम गर्राईरहेको जानकारी दिए ।

सामाजिक सञ्जालमा देखिने विभिन्न अफवाहलाई रोक्दै सद्भाव कायम गर्नुपर्ने गरि सार्वजनिक अपिल गर्न थालिएको छ। केहिदिनदेखि अशान्त बनेको तराई मधेसमा विस्तारै शान्ति स्थापनाका निम्ति नागरिक नै जागरुक बन्न थालेका छन्। यद्यपी वीरगञ्ज र सिरहाको गोलबजारलगायतका केही क्षेत्रमा भने निषेधाज्ञा अझै कायम रहेको प्रशासनले जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: शैलेन्द्र अधिकारीको तेस्रो उपन्यास ‘तेजस्’ सार्वजनिक
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । लेखक तथा अध्यापक शैलेन्द्र अधिकारीको तेस्रो उपन्यास ‘तेजस्’ सार्वजनिक भएको छ। शनिबार एक कार्यक्रमबीच बुद्धविहार काठमाडौँका भिक्षु कोण्डन्य, आख्यानकार एवं अनलाइनखबरका प्रधान सम्पादक बसन्त बस्नेत, संस्कृतिकर्मी नानी हेरा शाक्य, राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)का नेता मिलन पाण्डे र कवि रुपक अलंकारलले पुस्तकको संयुक्त विमोचन गरेका हुन्।

कार्यक्रममा भिक्षु कोण्डन्यले ‘तेजस्’मा राणाकालमा बौद्ध समुदायमाथि भएको दमन र भिक्षुहरूलाई देशनिकाला गरिएको प्रसंग तथा पञ्चायतकालमा उनीहरू स्वदेश फर्किएको इतिहासलाई समेटिएको बताए।

उपन्यासले भाषा, संस्कार र संस्कृतिको संरक्षणको सशक्त सन्देश दिएको उनको भनाइ थियो। विपश्यना र बौद्ध दर्शनका पक्षहरू पनि कथामा प्रभावकारी रूपमा समेटिएको भन्दै उनले उपन्यास सशक्त र पठनीय भएको बताए ।

आख्यानकार एवं अनलाइनखबरका प्रधान सम्पादक बस्नेतले ‘तेजस्’ काठमाडौँको भूगोल र इतिहास बुझ्न अत्यन्त उपयोगी कृति भएको बताए।

सेतो ख्याकको दृष्टिकोणबाट कथा भनिएकाले उपन्यास रहस्यमय बनेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले बौद्ध धर्ममाथि राज्यले विभिन्न कालखण्डमा गरेको उपेक्षा र दमनलाई पुस्तकले गहिराइका साथ उजागर गरेको उनको भनाइ थियो। ‘कान्तिपुर (काठमाडौँ) को भूगोल र इतिहासको यो एउटा टुर गाइड पुस्तक बनेको छ,’ उनले भने, ‘किताब स्वादको बनेको छ। संगठन नबनाइ एक्लै एक्लै काम गर्दा बिद्धस्टहरूलाई राज्यले कति सतायो भन्ने दस्तावेज हो यो किताब।

रास्वपा नेता पाण्डेले असन, वसन्तपुर, नेवार समुदाय र ख्याकसँग सम्बन्धित धेरै कम सुनिएका कथा पुस्तकमा समेटिएको उल्लेख गर्दै उपन्यासले काठमाडौँका सम्पदालाई हेर्ने आफ्नो दृष्टिकोण नै परिवर्तन गरेको बताए।

संस्कृतिविद् नानीहेरा शाक्यले उपन्यासले नेपाल मण्डलकालीन कान्तिपुर, वसन्तपुर, कुमारीघर र चित्लाङसम्मको परिवेशलाई जीवन्त रूपमा उतारेको बताइन्। नेवार समुदाय कसरी क्रमशः सीमान्तकृत भयो भन्ने विषयलाई संवेदनशील ढंगले प्रस्तुत गरिएको भन्दै उनले नेपाल भाषाका केही शब्दमा सामान्य त्रुटि रहेको पनि औंल्याइन्।

कवि रूपक अलंकारले अध्ययनशील लेखकका रूपमा अधिकारीको प्रशंसा गर्दै ‘तेजस्’ कुनै एक पात्रको कथा मात्र नभई समयसँगै बदलिएको काठमाडौँ, नेवारी संस्कृति र बौद्ध धर्मको रूपान्तरणको कथा भएको बताए। शाहकाल र त्यसपछिका राजनीतिक परिवर्तनले काठमाडौँ र बौद्ध परम्परामा पारेको प्रभावलाई उपन्यासले प्रभावशाली रूपमा चित्रण गरेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

लेखक शैलेन्द्र अधिकारीले उपन्यास लेख्ने क्रममा नेपालबाट बौद्ध भिक्षुहरू देशनिकाला गरिएको इतिहासले आफूलाई गहिरो रूपमा छोएको बताए। नेवारी समुदायको जीवन र संस्कृतिलाई नजिकबाट बुझ्न आफूले लामो समय अध्ययन र सहकार्य गरेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले इतिहास, मिथक र सामाजिक यथार्थलाई जोडेर ‘तेजस्’ तयार भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

शिखा बुक्सले प्रकाशन गरेको पुस्तकको मूल्य ७२५ रुपैयाँ तोकिएको छ।

articles.title: सद्भाव कायमम गर्न सुरक्षा निकायको आफ्नै योजना
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । सुनसरीको देवानगन्जमा आइतबार भएको दुई समूहबीचको झडपपछि विग्रिएको परिस्थिति सामान्य बन्दै गएको छ । सुनसरीबाट मधेसका जिल्लातर्फ परेको बाछिटा पनि कम हुँदै गएको छ ।

स्थिति सामान्य बन्दै गएपछि धनुषा, सिरहा, सुनसरी, सप्तरीमा र वीरगन्जमा लगाइएको कफ्र्यु हटाएर निषेधाज्ञा मात्र जारी गरिएको छ । विशेषगरी अहिले भइरहेको घटनामा सुरक्षा निकायको मूल्यांकन के छ ? अनि तनाव न्यूनीकरण र सद्भाव कायम गर्न सुरक्षा निकायले के गरिरहेको छ त ?

दुई समुदायबीच उत्पन्न तनाव मत्थर पार्न सुरक्षा निकायले विभिन्न रणनीति अपनाएको छ । त्यस मध्येको पहिलो रणनीति हो– उच्च अधिकारीहरूलाई फिल्डमा खटाउने । नेपाल प्रहरीले सुरक्षा व्यवस्था सुदृढ बनाउन ४ एआईजीसहित दुई दर्जनभन्दा बढी उच्च अधिकारीलाई कोशी र मधेश प्रदेशमा खटाएको छ । उनीहरूले त्यहाँको वस्तुस्थिति बुझेर केन्द्रमा रिपोर्ट पठाउने र त्यसैका आधारमा जनशक्ति खटाउने तयारी गरिएको छ ।

प्रहरीका उच्च अधिकारीहरु को कहाँ ?

प्रहरी अतिरिक्त महानिरीक्षक सिद्धिविक्रम शाहलाई बाँके, उमाप्रसाद चतुर्वेदीलाई कपिलवस्तु र ईश्वर कार्कीलाई सुनसरी पठाइएको छ । प्रहरी नायब महानिरीक्षक दिनेशकुमार आचार्यलाई सिरहा र अभिनारायण काफ्लेलाई सप्तरीमा खटाइएको छ ।

प्रहरी वरिष्ठ उपरीक्षक गोपालचन्द्र भट्टराईलाई सर्लाही, सोमेन्द्रसिंह राठौरलाई पर्सा, दीपशमशेर राणालाई रौतहट, नवराज अधिकारीलाई चितवन, कृष्णप्रसाद पंगेनीलाई महोत्तरी र होविन्द्र बोगटीलाई बारामा पठाइएको छ। त्यसैगरी, ज्ञानेन्द्रप्रसाद फुयाँललाई मोरङ, भुवनेश्वर तिवारीलाई धनुषा र अमरेन्द्रबहादुर सिंहलाई मधेस प्रदेशमा खटाइएको छ ।

उनीहरुले विकसित घटनाक्रमअनुसार सुरक्षा व्यवस्थापन गर्ने, जनशक्ति तथा स्रोतसाधन परिचालनको प्रभावकारिता मूल्यांकन गर्ने र आवश्यक नीति निर्देशन दिनेछन् । उनीहरूलाई सुरक्षा योजना कार्यान्वयन, सूचना संकलन र विश्लेषणलगायत जिम्मेवारी पनि दिइएको छ।

सुरक्षा चुक भएको निष्कर्ष

लगातार बसेका सुरक्षा बैठकले सुनसरी घटनामा सुरक्षा चुक भएको निष्कर्ष निकालेका छन्। सूचना संकलन र विश्लेषणमा सुरक्षा निकायले सन्तोषजनक काम गर्न नसकेको बैठकको निष्कर्ष छ । घटनालाई सामान्य रूपमा लिएर बेलैमा नियन्त्रणको प्रयास नगर्दा मानवीय तथा भौतिक क्षति बढेको पनि बैठकको विश्लेषण छ ।

यसैलाई मध्यनजर गरेर सुरक्षा निकायले सीमा क्षेत्रबाट आउने नयाँ व्यक्तिलाई निगरानीमा राखिएको छ । ड्रोनबाट हुने अनुगमनलाई पनि सक्रिय बनाइएको छ ।

दोस्रो सुरक्षा रणनीति हो–दुई पक्षलाई भेट हुन नदिने ।

सम्भावित जोखिम न्यूनीकरण गर्नका लागि तत्काल दुई पक्षलाई टाढै राख्ने गृह प्रशासनको तयारी छ ।

त्यसैगरी सुरक्षा निकायले बनाएको तेस्रो रणनीति हो– सुरक्षा फोर्सको तैनाथी ।

तनाव देखिएका कोशी र मधेशबाहेकका प्रदेशमा पनि अहिले सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई सतर्क अवस्थामा राखिएको छ ।

केही अप्ठ्यारो पर्ने अवस्था आएमा आवश्यक संख्यामा सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई तनाव देखिएका क्षेत्रमा पठाउने तयारी भइरहेको छ । तनाव न्यूनीकरणको चौंथो रणनीति हो– मठमन्दिर तथा मस्जिदहरू रहेका क्षेत्रमा अतिरिक्त सुरक्षा सतर्कता । फिल्डमा खटिन नपर्ने सुरक्षा फोर्सलाई धार्मिक स्थलहरूमा खटाइएको छ ।

अहिलेसम्म प्रहरीले साम्प्रदायिक÷सामाजिक सद्भावमा खलल पुरÞ्याएको भन्दै प्रहरीले ६५ जना व्यक्तिहरू पक्राउ गरेको छ । सिरहमा ५ जना, धनुषामा ४५ जना, सर्लाही ५ जना , महोतरीमा २ जना ,पर्सामा १ जना,सप्तरीमा १ जना ,सुनसरीमा २ जना ब्यक्तिहरु प्रहरीले प्रकाउ गरेको छ । सुरक्षा निकायले कुनै पनि किसिमका भ्रामक सामग्री सम्प्रेषण नगर्न तथा अनावश्यक उत्तेजित नहुन समेत भनेको छ ।

पाँचौँ सुरक्षा रणनीति हो– समन्वयको । प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीको संयोजकत्वमा जनप्रतिनिधि, धर्मगुरु तथा सुरक्षा निकायले छलफल र समन्वय गरिरहेका छन् ।साथै जनप्रतिनिधि र स्थानीय बासिन्दालाई गाउँ टोलमा नयाँ मान्छे आएमा सुरक्षा निकायलाई खबर गर्न पनि भनिएको छ ।

छैठौं सुरक्षा रणनीतिअनुसार सीमा नाकाबाट घुसपैठ हुनसक्ने परिस्थितिको जोखिम आकलन गर्दै त्यहाँ पनि सतर्कता अपनाइएको छ । सबै सुरक्षा रणनीति प्रभावकारी रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्न गृहसचिवको संयोजकत्वमा प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकसहितको कमान्ड फोर्सले एकीकृत सूचनासमेत संकलन गरिरहेको छ ।

सुनसरी घटनाबारे अनुसन्धान भइरहेकाले प्रतिवेदन नआएसम्म दोषी किटान गर्न नसकिने अवस्था रहेको सुरक्षा निकायको भनाइ छ ।

articles.title: निर्मल पुर्जासहित सबै आरोहीको निधन, कस्ता थिए कीर्तिमानी ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । कीर्तिमानी आरोही निर्मल पुर्जासहितका १० जनाकै निधन भएको छ। बिहीबारदेखि हराइरहेका पुर्जाको निधन भएको उनी संस्थापक रहेको संस्था एलिट एक्सपेडले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत पुष्टि गरेको छ। विश्वविख्यात पुर्जाको निधनले विश्वभर शोकको अवस्था बनेको छ ।

’आज, अत्यन्तै दुःख र मर्माहत हृदयका साथ हामी यो पुष्टि गर्दछौं कि ब्रोड पिकमा गएको हिमपहिरोमा परी निर्मल “निम्सदाइ“ पुर्जाले दुःखद रूपमा आफ्नो ज्यान गुमाउनुभएको छ। साथै, यस अभियानमा संलग्न अन्य सदस्यहरू पनि जीवित रहन नसकेको पुष्टि भएको छ।’ विश्व कीर्तिमानका लागि परिचित पुर्जासहित १० जनाले नै ज्यान गुमाएको घटनाले विश्वभर शोक मनाउन थालिएको छ।

१० जनाले नै गुमाए ज्यान

बिहीबार बिहान करिब ६ हजार ७ सय मिटरको उचाईमा पुगेपछि खसेको हिमपहिरोमा परी उनीहरु वेपत्ता भएका थिए। आरोहण दलको नेतृत्व गरेका पुर्जासहित विभिन्न देशमा आरोहीको खोजी तीब्र पारिएको थियो। हिमपहिरोमा परी ज्यान गुमाउनेहरुमा नेपालका पुरबहादुर गुरूङ, किली पेम्बा शेर्पा ’किलु’, निमा शेर्पा र नवाङ थिन्डु शेर्पा, ओमानका नधिरा अहमद अब्दुल्लाह अल हार्थी, अमेरिकी आरोही मालोरी गाइस, पाकिस्तानका सोहेल साखी र चीनका वाङ जोङ रहेका छन्। तीन जनाको शव शुक्रबार नै फेला परेको थियो भने पुर्जासहित अन्यको निधनको पुष्टी आजमात्रे भएको हो।

निर्मलको भावुक पोस्ट

निर्मल पुर्जाले ब्रोक पिक चढ्नुअघि सामाजिक सञ्जालमा लामो सन्देश लेखेका थिए। उनले ब्रोड पिक चढ्ने योजना नभएको समेत उल्लेख गरेका थिए। तर, उनले प्रार्थना गर्दै लेखेका थिए, ‘ब्रोड पिक– म तिमीसँग केवल एउटा कुरा माग्छु–मलाई सुरक्षित रूपमा माथि पुग्न र फेरि सुरक्षित रूपमा फर्किन देऊ ।’ यहि सन्देशमा उनले कुनै पनि हिमाललाई हल्का रुपमा नलिने जिकिर गरेका पुर्जा अब कहिल्यै नफर्किने गरि अस्थाएका छन्।

‘बेसक्याम्पबाट पहिलो पाइला चाल्नेबित्तिकै मेरो सम्पूर्ण समर्पण त्यही अभियानमा हुन्छ । सधैं त्यस्तै थियो । सधैं त्यस्तै रहनेछ,’ पुर्जाको अन्तिम सन्देश समेत यहि बन्न पुगेको छ ।

पुर्जाले सन् २०१९ मा विश्वका ८ हजार मिटरभन्दा अग्ला सबै १४ हिमाल केवल ६ महिनाभन्दा केही बढी अवधिमा आरोहण गरेर विश्व कीर्तिमान कायम गरेका थिए । ८ हजार मिटर माथिका हिमाल आरोहण रेकर्ड हेर्दा यस पटक ब्रोड पिक चढेका भए चोयुबाहेक ८ हजार मिटर माथिका १४ वटै हिमाल विनाअक्सिजन दुई पटक आरोहण गर्ने विश्व कीर्तिमान उनको नाममा दर्ज हुने निश्चित थियो । अघिल्लो सातामात्र उनले पाकिस्तानको गसेरब्रम २ आरोहण गरी ५७औं आरोहण पूरा गरेका थिए । यस पटक ब्रोड पिक आरोहणको योजनामा भने नरहेको पनि उनले स्टाटसमा उल्लेख गरेका थिए ।

बेलायती सेनादेखि हिमालसम्म

म्याग्दीका निर्मल पुर्जा १८ वर्षको उमेरमै बेलायती सेनामा भर्ति भएका थिए। लामो समय बेलायतमै विताएका उनी बेलायती नागरिक समेत हुन्।पुर्जा १८ वर्षको उमेरमा सन् २००३ मा बेलायती सेनामा भर्ती भएका थिए । त्यसपछि सन् २००९ मा उनी रोयल मरिन्समा आबद्ध भए ।

उनले आफ्ना बुबा र दाजुहरूको बाटो पछ्याएका थिए । उनका बुबा र दाजुहरू सबै गोर्खा सैनिक थिए । गोर्खा सैनिकहरू नेपाली सैनिकहरूको प्रसिद्ध समूह हुन्, जसले २०० वर्षभन्दा बढी समयदेखि बेलायती सेनामा सेवा गर्दै आएका छन् ।

१६ वर्ष बेलायती सेनामा विताएका उनी पर्वतारोहणसम्बन्धि विशेष रुची राख्ने गर्थे। उनको असाधारण पर्वतारोहण उपलब्धिका लागि सन् २०१८ मा तत्कालीन बेलायती महारानी एलिजाबेथ द्वितीयले एमबीई (मेम्बर अफ द अर्डर अफ तजभ ब्रिटिस इम्पायर) सम्मान प्रदान गरेकी थिइन्। यो उत्कृष्ठ उपलब्धिका लागि प्रदान गरिने नागरिक सम्मान भएको बताइन्छ। उनी नेपाली मुलका बेलायती नागरिक भएपनि उनको निधनले नेपाल शोकमा डुबेको छ।

प्रधानमन्त्रीको श्रद्धाञ्जली

प्रधानमन्त्री वालेन्द्र शाहले निर्मल पुर्जासहित ब्रोड पिक आरोहणको क्रममा ज्यान गुमाउनेप्रति श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गरेका छन्। प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले लेखेका छन्, ’विश्वको १२औँ अग्लो हिमाल, पाकिस्तानको काराकोरम पर्वत–शृङ्खलामा अवस्थित ८,०५१ मिटर अग्लो ‘ब्रोड पिक’मा विश्व कीर्तिमानधारी निर्मल पुर्जा (निम्स दाइ) सहित छ जना नेपाली तथा अन्य चार विदेशी आरोहीहरूको दुःखद निधनले स्तब्ध बनाएको छ ।

निर्मल पुर्जा लगायत सम्पूर्ण दिवङ्गत आरोहीहरूको भौतिक यात्रा मात्रै रोकिएको हो, तर उहाँहरूको साहस, समर्पण र योगदानको इतिहास सधैँ प्रेरणायुक्त र जीवित रहिरहनेछ ।

सम्पूर्ण दिवङ्गत आरोहीहरूप्रति भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जली ।’ उसोतः प्रधानमन्त्री शाहले हिमाल आरोहण शिखर चुम्ने यात्रा मात्रै नभई साहस, अनुशासन, त्याग र मानवीय सीमालाई चुनौती दिने अदम्य आत्मविश्वासको सर्वोच्च अभिव्यक्ति भन्दै हिमालले गौरव दिने तर, कहिलेकाँही आफ्नै काखमा सधैका लागि अंगालेर राख्ने बताएका छन्।

उनीहरुको समर्पणको इतिहास कहिल्यै नमर्ने भनेका शाहले शोक व्यक्त गरेका हुन्। उसोतः निर्मलसहितका आरोहीको निधनमा नेपाल शोकमा डुबेको छ भने विश्वभर नै यसको चर्चा र शोक व्यक्तको क्रम चलिरहेको छ।

articles.title: नेपालीलाई झन कडा ! २० हजार डलरको तगारो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित ५० देशका नागरिकले अब अमेरिकी बी–वान र बी–टु भिजिटर भिसाका लागि अधिकतम २० हजार अमेरिकी डलरसम्म धरौटी राख्नुपर्ने भएको छ । अगस्ट ३ देखि लागू हुने नयाँ व्यवस्थाले भिसा आवेदन प्रक्रिया थप कडा र खर्चिलो बन्ने भएको छ ।

अमेरिका जाने योजना बनाइरहनुभएको छ ? विशेषगरी व्यापार वा घुमघामका लागि बी–वान वा बी–टु भिजिटर भिसा लिने सोचमा हुनुहुन्छ भने अब एउटा ठूलो परिवर्तनबारे तपाईल जान्नै पर्ने भएको छ । अमेरिकी सरकारले भिजिटर भिसामा लागू गर्दै आएको धरौटी प्रणालीलाई अब स्थायी बनाउने निर्णय गरेको छ ।

योसँगै धरौटी रकम पनि उल्लेख्य रूपमा बढाएको छ । अगस्ट ३, २०२६ अर्थात् पर्सी सोमवारदेखि लागू हुने नयाँ नियमअनुसार नेपालसहित तोकिएका ५० देशका बी–वान र बी–टु भिसा आवेदकले अब १० हजार, १५ हजार वा २० हजार अमेरिकी डलरसम्म धरौटी राख्नुपर्नेछ । यसअघि परीक्षण कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत अधिकतम १५ हजार डलरसम्मको व्यवस्था थियो ।

सामान्यतया कन्सुलर अधिकारीले १५ हजार डलर धरौटी निर्धारण गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ । तर आवेदकको भ्रमणको उद्देश्य, रोजगारी, आम्दानी र अन्य अवस्थाका आधारमा यो रकम १० हजार वा २० हजार डलरसम्म हुन सक्छ । यो व्यवस्था पहिलो पटक अगस्ट २०२५ मा परीक्षणका रूपमा सुरु गरिएको थियो ।

अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार एक वर्षको अनुभवले यो प्रणालीले भिसाका शर्त पालना गराउन प्रभावकारी भूमिका खेलेको देखिएको छ । यसो गर्दा उच्च ओभरस्टे दर, कमजोर सूचना आदानप्रदान, पहिचान प्रमाणीकरण र यात्रा कागजातको सुरक्षामा कमजोरी भएका देशमाथि कूटनीतिक दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्य पनि यसमा रहेको मन्त्रालयको भनाइ छ ।

भिसा प्रक्रिया कसरी शुरु हुन्छ ?

सबैभन्दा पहिले अन्य गैरआवासीय भिसा आवेदनजस्तै अन्तर्वार्ताको समय लिनुपर्नेछ र नियमित भिसा शुल्क तिर्नुपर्नेछ । त्यसपछि कन्सुलर अधिकारीले सबै योग्यता पुगेको र तपाईं तोकिएको देशको नागरिक भएको ठहर गरेमा भिसा तत्काल जारी हुँदैन । अध्यागमन तथा राष्ट्रियता ऐनको धारा २२१ जी अन्तर्गत भिसा अस्थायी रूपमा रोक्का गरिन्छ । त्यसपछि गृह सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयको धरौटी फाराम र सरकारी विद्युतीय भुक्तानी प्रणालीमार्फत धरौटी बुझाउन भनिन्छ । यो रकम आवेदक आफैंले वा तेस्रो पक्षले पनि तिर्न सक्नेछन् ।

धरौटी प्राप्त भएपछि अन्तिम समीक्षा हुनेछ । स्वीकृति पाए तीनदेखि १२ महिनासम्म वैध रहने सिंगल वा मल्टिपल इन्ट्री भिसा जारी हुन सक्नेछ । भिसामै धरौटी बुझाइएको विवरण पनि उल्लेख हुनेछ । अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयका अनुसार यो कार्यक्रमको उद्देश्य रकम उठाउनु मात्रे होइन । एक वर्षको परीक्षणले यात्रुहरूलाई भिसाका शर्त पालना गराउन यो प्रणाली प्रभावकारी देखिएको मन्त्रालयको निष्कर्ष छ ।

त्यस्तै उच्च ओभरस्टे दर, कमजोर सूचना आदानप्रदान, पहिचान प्रमाणीकरण र यात्रा कागजातको सुरक्षामा कमजोरी भएका देशमाथि कूटनीतिक दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्य पनि यसमा रहेको बताइएको छ । यद्यपि धरौटी फिर्ता हुने व्यवस्था पनि छ । त्यसका लागि भिसा बाहकले अनधिकृत रूपमा काम गर्नु हुँदैन, अनुमति अवधिभित्र अमेरिका छाड्नुपर्छ वा आवश्यक परे समयमै बसाइ अवधि थप अथवा भिसा स्टेटस परिवर्तनका लागि आवेदन दिनुपर्छ ।

सरकारी प्रणालीले सबै शर्त पालना भएको पुष्टि गरेपछि धरौटी स्वतः रद्द हुनेछ र पूरा रकम कुनै ब्याजबिना फिर्ता हुनेछ । तर यदि अनुमति अवधिभन्दा बढी अमेरिका बसियो, आवेदन ढिलो गरियो, अस्वीकृतिपछि १० दिनभित्र पनि अमेरिका छाडिएन वा शरण अथवा अन्य मानवीय संरक्षणका लागि आवेदन दिइयो भने धरौटी रकम स्वतः जफत हुन सक्छ । यस्तो अवस्थामा अन्तिम निर्णय भने होमल्याण्ड सेक्युरिटीले गर्नेछ । एउटा रोचक तथ्य के भने परीक्षण कार्यक्रम सुरु गर्दा एक वर्षमा करिब दुई हजार आवेदक मात्रै धरौटीको दायरामा पर्ने अनुमान गरिएको थियो ।

तर वास्तविक संख्या झन्डै २० हजार पुग्यो । तीमध्ये करिब आधाले मात्रै धरौटी बुझाए । त्यसको प्रभाव भिसा जारी हुने दरमै देखियो । कार्यक्रम लागू भएका देशका नागरिकका लागि बी–श्रेणी भिसा जारी हुने दर पहिलो १० महिनामै अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा ८३ प्रतिशतले घटेको अमेरिकी विदेश मन्त्रालयले जनाएको छ ।

यदि तपाईं अमेरिका भ्रमणको तयारीमा हुनुहुन्छ भने पक्कै पनि अब भिसा आवेदनको चेकलिस्टमा एउटा नयाँ कुरा धरौटी थपिएको छ । भिसाका लागि आवेदन दिनुअघि यो नयाँ व्यवस्था बुझ्न एकदमै महत्वपूर्ण छ । त्यसैले आवेदन अघि यी नियमहरू राम्रोसँग बुझेर मात्रै प्रक्रिया अगाडि बढाउनु उपयुक्त हुनेछ ।

articles.title: मलेसिया रोजगारीमा सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द लोकतान्त्रिक एसोसियसन
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । मलेसिया रोजगारीमा एकाधिकार (सिण्डिकेट) लगाउन खोजिएको भन्दै वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न संगठनहरूले आन्दोलनको चेतावनी दिएका छन् । नेपाल लोकतान्त्रिक वैदेशिक रोजगार एसोसियसनको आयोजनामा शुक्रबार काठमाडौंमा वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूले यस्तो चेतावनी दिएका हुन् ।

एसोसियसनले मलेसिया रोजगारीमा केही व्यवसायीहरूले सिण्डिकेट लगाउन खोजेको भन्दै छलफल आयोजना गरेको महासचिव सुमनराज पाण्डेले बताए । ‘केही व्यवसायीहरूको निहित स्वार्थमा मलेसिया रोजगारीमा सिण्डिकेट लगाउन खोजिएको छ । यो विल्कुल गलत छ,’ महासचिव पाण्डेले भने, आजबाट सरोकारवालाहरूसँग छलफल शुरू भएको छ । सिण्डिकेट लागू भयो भने हामी आन्दोलनमा उत्रन्छौं । एसोसियसनले वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द पहल नगरे एक्लै भएपनि संघर्षमा उत्रने तयारी गरेको छ ।

छलफलमा एसोसियसनका पूर्वअध्यक्ष प्रज्ञान न्यौपाने, कुमुद खनाल, दीपक थापा, नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघका निवर्तमान अध्यक्ष भुवनसिंह गुरूङ,संघका पूर्वमहासचिव मेघनाथ भुर्तेल, प्रगतिशिल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी मञ्चका उपाध्यक्ष सरिता घले, नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायिक गणतान्त्रिक मञ्चका अध्यक्ष धनलाल जैशी, एकीकृत वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संगठनका कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष मीन प्रसाद गोलेसहित तामाङ समान, नेवा समाज, मगर समाज, महिला संघलगायत थुप्रै घटक संस्थाहरू सहभागी थिए ।

उनीहरूले व्यवसायीहरूको छाता संस्था वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघको भूमिकामाथि पनि प्रश्न उठाएका छन् । एसोसियसनका कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष सुवर्ण लामाले सिण्डिकेटविरूद्द संघको ध्यानाकर्षण गराउने बताए ।

articles.title: स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति कौडीमा एनसेलले हात पारेपछि हंगामा, भुपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउपछि चासो बढ्यो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। नेपाल प्रहरीको सीआइबीले भण्डारीलाई अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरेको छ। भण्डारी किन पक्राउ परे? स्मार्ट प्रकरणमा भण्डारीको भूमिका के? चासो देखिन्छन्।

नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। स्मार्ट सेलको सम्पत्ति बेचेर राज्यलाई हानी नोक्सानी पु¥याएको आरोपमा उनी पक्राउ परेका हुन्। तत्कालीन समयमा रेखा शर्मा सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधिमन्त्री हुँदा भण्डारी विज्ञको रूपमा उनको सचिवालयमा नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

सचिवालयमा विज्ञ भनिएका भण्डारीलाई टेरामक्स प्रकरणले चिठ्ठा नै पर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। त्यसपछि टेरामक्स प्रकरणमा प्राधिकारणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनाल भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दाका कारण निलम्बित भएपछि उनले प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष पदमा सहजै पुग्ने स्थिति निर्माण गरे। तर, भण्डारी अध्यक्ष बनेपछि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा वेच्ने काम भएको बताइन्छ। राज्यको नाममा आईसकेको टेलिकमको सम्पत्तिलाई निजी कम्पनी एनसेललाई कौडीको भाउमा बेच्न सघाएको आरोपमा भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका हुन्।

के भन्यो सीआइबीले ?

नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)ले शुक्रबार ललितपुरको धापाखेलबाट पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ। उनलाई स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरिएको बताइएको छ। सीआईबीले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आएको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति बेइमानीपूर्वक सरकारको हक टुटाउन काम गराएको आरोपमा भण्डारी माथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको थियो।

दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० वैशाखमा अनुमति पाएको थियो। तर अनुमतिपत्र नवीकरण नगरेपछि स्मार्ट टेलिकमको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भएको थियो। यसरी सरकारको नाममा पुगिसकेको सम्पत्तिलाई बेचबिखन गर्नका निम्ति सघाएको आरोप भण्डारीमाथि समेत लागेको छ। प्राधिकरण नियामक निकाय समेत भएकाले पनि उनीमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने माग पहिलेदेखि नै उठ्दै आएको थियो । यता, ब्युरोले वैशाखमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमका तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध निर्देशक सर्वेश जोशीलाई पक्राउ गरिसकेको छ।

स्मार्टमा एनसेलको चलाखी

इजाजत खारेजीपछि विवादास्पद रूपमा सम्पत्ति लिलाम बिक्री भएको स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा निजी क्षेत्रको दूरसञ्चार सेवाप्रदायक कम्पनी एनसेल, त्यहाँका प्रमुख लगानीकर्ता र राजनीतिक नेतृत्वबीच शंकास्पद सम्बन्ध देखिएको भन्दै सीआइबीले अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ।

स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति बिक्रीबाट प्रमुख लाभग्राही एनसेल देखिएको छ। नेपाल दूरसञ्चार नियमावलीको नियम १० क मा एकै कम्पनीले एकभन्दा बढी दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकको अनुमति नपाउने उल्लेख छ। तर एनसेलमा लगानी गरेकाहरुले नै गैरकानुनीरूपले लिलामी गरिएको स्मार्ट टेलिकममा पनि लगानी सकारेकोे सीआईबीको ठहर छ ।

अहिले अनुसन्धानमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सेयर बिक्री, सेयर स्वामित्वको इतिहास, बैंक ऋण, सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न कारोबार हेरिएको छ। प्रहरीले स्मार्ट टेलिकम, त्यसका सेयरधनी, सम्पत्ति व्यवस्थापन, उपकरण बिक्री र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका आर्थिक सम्बन्धबारे अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रक्रियाभन्दा अगाडि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकम र एनसेलबीच सम्बन्ध देखिन्छ। यही आधारमा एनसेलसँग जोडिएका केही उच्च तहका व्यक्तिलाई पनि छानबिनको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ। स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रकरणमा एनसेलको नेपालस्थित सञ्चालकहरू सतिशलाल आचार्य, भावना सिंह श्रेष्ठ र सचिनलाल आचार्य पनि अनुसन्धानको राडारमै रहेका छन्।

दुरसञ्चार ऐन र स्वार्थको द्वन्द्ध

दुरसञ्चार ऐन २०५३ को दफा नंवर ३३ को उपदफा १ बमोजिम नेपाल सरकारले स्वामित्वमा आएको सम्पत्ति पूर्व अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिले उपदफा (३) बमोजिम निर्धारण गरिने मूल्य नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाई पुनः अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरी दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न सक्नेछ भनिएको छ ।

फेरि उपदफा २ बमोजिमको मूल्य निर्धारण गर्ने प्रयोजनको लागि नेपाल सरकारले प्राधिकरणको परामर्श लिई बमोजिम विशेषज्ञ व्यक्तिहरुको एक समिति गठन गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । तर, प्राधिकारणले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकम एनसेललाई बेच्ने कुरा नै असंगत, पदीय दुरुपयोग र भ्रष्टाचार हुने दाबीहरु सार्वजनिक भइरहेका छन्।

यस्तो अवस्थामा प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बनेका भण्डारीले पनि कानूनको उल्लङ्घन गर्दै स्मार्टको पक्षमा काम गरेकाले उनी अनुसन्धानमा तानिएका हुन्। तत्कालीन माओवादी केन्द्रबाट सञ्चारमन्त्री बनेकी शर्माले अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेका भण्डारीमाथि पदीय दुरुपयोगको गम्भीर आरोप लाग्दै गर्दा नियुक्ति दिने शर्मामाथि समेत केहिले प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। कतै यो सबै सेटिङमै त भएन?

प्रहरीले अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने बाटो यसतर्फ समेत केन्द्रित गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिन थालिएको छ। यद्यपी शर्मामाथि यस्ता आरोप भने सार्वजनिक रुपमा लागेको देखिन्न। तर, सचिवालयको विज्ञ भनिएको कर्मचारीलाई अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेपछि कानून मिचेको देखिदा उनीमाथि समेत यस्तो प्रश्न स्वभाविक बन्न पुगेको छ ।

articles.title: ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप नेपाल प्रवेश : जेम होम कलेक्सन आधिकारिक वितरक नियुक्त
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं। भारतको अग्रणी होम टेक्सटाइल कम्पनी ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गरेको छ। कम्पनीले नेपालका लागि आफ्ना होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको एकमात्र आधिकारिक वितरकको रूपमा जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेडलाई नियुक्त गरेको घोषणा गरेको छ। यस सहकार्यसँगै नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अब ट्राइडेन्टका प्रिमियम बेड लिनेन, बाथ लिनेन, तौलियालगायतका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू आधिकारिक तथा भरपर्दो माध्यमबाट प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्।

यसअघि नेपाली बजारमा ट्राइडेन्टका उत्पादनहरू प्रायः अनौपचारिक माध्यमबाट भित्रिने गरेकोमा यस नियुक्तिपछि गुणस्तर र प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितता हुने कम्पनीहरूको दाबी छ। यस साझेदारीले नेपालमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रियस्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको पहुँच विस्तार गर्ने र नेपाली ग्राहकहरूलाई विश्वस्तरीय गुणस्तर, आधिकारिक आपूर्ति शृंखला तथा उत्कृष्ट ग्राहक सेवा उपलब्ध गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको छ।

जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेड विगत ३० वर्षदेखि नेपालको फ्लोरिङ तथा फर्निसिङ क्षेत्रमा सक्रिय रहेको कम्पनी हो। यसले आतिथ्य र खुद्रा दुवै बजारका लागि विविध गुणस्तरीय उत्पादनहरू निरन्तर आपूर्ति गर्दै आएको छ। यही दीर्घकालीन बजार अनुभव र स्थापित वितरण सञ्जालका कारण कम्पनीलाई ट्राइडेन्टको आधिकारिक साझेदारका रूपमा छनोट गरिएको बताइएको छ।

ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपको स्थापना सन् १९९० मा भारतीय उद्यमी पद्मश्री राजिन्दर गुप्ताले पञ्जाबबाट सुरु गरेका थिए। सुरुमा एउटा मात्र धागो उत्पादन एकाइबाट सुरु भएको यो समूह हाल विश्वकै सबैभन्दा ठूला टेरी तौलिया उत्पादक र समग्र होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादकहरूमध्ये एक बनेको आर्थिक हिसाबले हेर्ने हो भने पछिल्लो प्रतिवेदन अनुसार ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले आर्थिक वर्ष २०२६ मा ६५ अर्ब २१ करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँ बराबरको आम्दानी हासिल गरेको थियो, जुन अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा सामान्य घटेको भए पनि खुद नाफा भने बढेको थियो।

चालु आर्थिक वर्षको हालसालैको प्रगति हेर्दा पनि, पहिलो त्रैमासमा आम्दानी १ हजार ८ सय ३० करोड रुपैयाँ पुगेको र खुद नाफा ५५ प्रतिशतले वृद्धि भएको देखिन्छ। कम्पनीको समग्र आकारका सन्दर्भमा हेर्दा, ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप इन्डियामा हाल १६ हजार ३ सय तीनजना कर्मचारी कार्यरत रहेका छन् र यसको बजार पूँजीकरण करिब १।३२ बिलियन डलर बराबर रहेको पाइन्छ। समूह लामो समयदेखि आफूलाई एक बिलियन डलरभन्दा बढी मूल्यको वैश्विक व्यापारिक समूहको रूपमा चिनाउँदै आएको छ, जसको होम टेक्सटाइल, कागज र रसायन क्षेत्रमा सशक्त उपस्थिति रहेको दाबी गरिन्छ।

यसआधिकारिक वितरण सम्झौतापछि नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितताका साथ प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन् भने होटल तथा रिसोर्ट जस्ता आतिथ्य व्यवसायहरूले पनि विश्वसनीय आपूर्ति स्रोत भेट्टाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ। साथै यसले नेपालको होम फर्निसिङ बजारमा स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा र गुणस्तर सुधारमा समेत योगदान पुर्‍याउने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

articles.title: मेची राजमार्ग ठप्प ! सडक बन्द हुँदा बिरामीदेखि ढुवानीसम्म संकट
articles.summary:
इलाम । मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलाम माइखोला राजदुवालीकमाथि सडक अवरुद्ध भएको तीन सात भयो । सडक खुल्ने अझै छाँटकाँट छैन । सडक बन्द भएपछि इलाम मात्र हैन पुर्वी पहाडी जिल्ला पाँचथर ताप्लेजुङ लगायतका स्थानीयलाई समेत सास्ती भएको छ ।

मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलामको माइखोला (राजदुवाली) माथिको सडक भासिएर तीन सातादेखि अवरुद्ध हुँदा इलामसँगै पाँचथर र ताप्लेजुङका नागरिकले सास्ती भोगिरहेका छन् । सडक बन्द भएपछि सवारी साधन वारिपारि नै रोकिने गरेका छन् भने यात्रुहरू करिब एक किलोमिटर भिरको बाटो पैदल हिँड्न बाध्य छन् ।

बिरामीलाई जनपथ प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी र नेपाली सेनाले स्टे«चरमार्फत वारपार गराइरहेका छन् भने एम्बुलेन्स पनि दुवैतर्फबाट सेवा दिन बाध्य छन् । अत्यावश्यक खाद्यान्न, ग्यास र तरकारी ढुवानीसमेत प्रभावित बनेको छ । इलाम नगरपालिकाले सरोकारवाला निकायसँग छलफल गरी पुनः इलामलाई संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ ।

राजदुवाली खण्डको पहिरो नियन्त्रण, ट्रस्ट पुल मर्मत तथा जोरकलश–हर्कटे सडक स्तरोन्नतिको लागि २४ करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको ठेक्का जे एन्ड जे निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले २०८४ असारसम्म सम्पन्न गर्ने गरी लिएको भएपनि हालसम्म समग्रमा १८–२० प्रतिशत मात्र काम भएको सडक डिभिजन कार्यालयले जनाएको छ । स्थानीयले मुख्य सडकभन्दा वैकल्पिक सडक तत्काल सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन माग गरेका छन् ।

गत वर्ष तीन महिनासम्म संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गरिए पनि प्रभावकारी काम नभएको भन्दै स्थानीय आक्रोशित छन् । सरकारले सडक बनाउन नसके इलामेली आफैंले श्रमदान र चन्दा उठाएर सडक तथा पुल निर्माण गर्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

सडक अवरुद्धकै कारण बिरामीले समयमै उपचार नपाएर ज्यान गुमाउनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको भन्दै तत्काल समाधानको माग गरिएको छ ।

उता वैकल्पिक सडकका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिने सिमलगोलाई–तिल्केनी तथा केचना–कञ्चनजंघा सडकको बेलासी–भन्ज्याङ खण्ड पनि निर्माणमा ढिलाइका कारण सञ्चालन योग्य छैन । माइजोगमाई र पुवा खोलाका पुल गत वर्षको बाढीले बगाएपछि अहिलेसम्म पुनर्निर्माण हुन सकेको छैन । यस वर्ष बजेटमै इलामलाई बेवास्ता गरिएको भन्दै स्थानीयले सरकारसँग तत्काल सडक सञ्चालनको सुनिश्चितता गर्न माग गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: बौद्धनाथमा अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिमा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप, कसले रोक्यो सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको नियुक्ति पत्र ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति तीन महिनादेखि अध्यक्षविहीन छ । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालय मातहतको यो महत्वपूर्ण निकायमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको सिफारिस भइसके पनि राजनीतिक स्वार्थका कारण नियुक्तिले अझै पूर्णता पाउन सकेको छैन । अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको निर्णय भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिँदा सरकारको नियतमाथि नै प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ ।

गत असार १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयअनुसार संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालयले बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिको अध्यक्षमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामालाई नियुक्त गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर विडम्बना, निर्णय भएको यति समय बितिसक्दा पनि लामाले नियुक्तिपत्र पाएका छैनन् ।

समितिका अध्यक्षसहित पाँच पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरिए पनि अध्यक्ष लामाबाहेक सबै सदस्यले नियुक्तिपत्र बुझिसकेका छन् । अध्यक्षलाई मात्रै रोक्नुको कारण काठमाडौं–३ का रास्वपा सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे रहेको आरोप छ ।

स्थानीयका अनुसार सांसद पाण्डेले आफ्ना निकट व्यक्तिलाई अध्यक्ष बनाउन दबाब दिएपछि लामाको नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिएको हो । लामो समयदेखि समिति नेतृत्वविहीन हुँदा गुठियारदेखि स्थानीय सरोकारवालासम्म सरकारसँग जवाफ माग्न थालेका छन् । उनीहरूको चेतावनी छ, ‘रास्वपाभित्रको जुंगाको लडाइँको छायाँ बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिमा पार्न मिल्दैन ।’

दुई कार्यकाल सफलतापूर्वक अध्यक्षको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको पुनः नियुक्तिका लागि गुठियार, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न संघसंस्था र बुद्धिजीवीहरूले एकमत सिफारिस गरेका थिए । स्थानीयका अनुसार लामा सबैले स्वीकार गरेका र समन्वयकारी क्षमता भएका व्यक्ति हुन् । अध्यक्ष नहुँदा बौद्धनाथमा प्रशासनिक कामदेखि सामाजिक, धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा विकास निर्माणका गतिविधि प्रभावित भएका छन् । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिले यहाँका विभिन्न धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक संघसंस्थाबीच समन्वय गर्दै आएको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका पनि अहिले नेतृत्व अभावकै कारण कमजोर बनेको छ ।

अलमलमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा

अध्यक्षमा नियुक्ति भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र नपाउँदा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा अन्योलमा परेका छन् । नियुक्ति भइसकेको व्यक्तिलाई नै बदर गराएर अर्को व्यक्तिलाई ल्याउने प्रयास सांसद पाण्डेले गरिरहेको स्थानीयको आरोप छ ।

उनीहरू भन्छन्, ‘सर्वस्वीकार्य व्यक्तिको नियुक्ति रोक्नु सरकारकै लागि ‘ब्याकफायर’ हुन सक्छ ।’ यसअघि पनि सरकार विभिन्न नियुक्ति र निर्णयका कारण विवादमा परिसकेको छ । धार्मिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संस्थामा राजनीतिक भागबन्डा होइन, योग्य र सबैले स्वीकार गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई नेतृत्व दिनुपर्ने स्थानीयको जोड छ । यही विषयलाई लिएर काठमाडौं–३ का सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे र संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री खडकराज पौडेल ९गणेश० बीच पनि मतभेद उत्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ ।

समितिका पाँच सदस्यमा विशाल लामा, निर्भिक्ता थिङ लामा, सेनाङ ग्याम्जो तामाङ, रोशनकुमार श्रेष्ठ र मणिभद्र पोखरेल नियुक्त भइसकेका छन् । तर अध्यक्षको नियुक्तिपत्र अझै रोकिँदा बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति नेतृत्वविहीन अवस्थामै अल्झिएको छ र राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपको आरोप झन् गहिरिँदै गएको छ ।

articles.title: पूजारी भन्छन्– बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको भ्रमले दर्शनार्थी घटे
articles.summary:
म्याग्दी । म्याग्दीको बेनी नगरपालिका ९ स्थित देशकै ऐतिहासिक र धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको गलेश्वरधाममा यस वर्षको साउन महिनामा विगतका वर्षको तुलनामा भक्तजनको चहलपहलमा कमि आएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यताका कारण पनि दर्शनार्थीहरुको कमी आएको हो ।

साउन महिना भगवान शिवको अत्यन्त प्रिय महिना भएकाले यस अवधिमा शिवको आराधना, रुद्राभिषेक, बेलपत्र चढाउने तथा जल चढाउनु विशेष फलदायी मानिन्छ । तर बृहस्पति अन्ध भएकै कारण मन्दिरमा दर्शन गर्न हुँदैन भन्ने भ्रम फैलिएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यतालाई लिएर दर्शनसमेत गर्न नहुने भन्ने भ्रमका कारण भक्तजनको संख्या घटेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालयका गलेश्वरधामका मूल पुजारी चन्द्रमणि आचार्यका अनुसार धार्मिक शास्त्रमा भगवानको दर्शन र पूजा–अर्चना गर्न कुनै निषेध गरिएको छैन । बरु साउन महिनामा शिवको आराधना गर्दा विशेष पुण्य प्राप्त हुने धार्मिक विश्वास छ ।

गलेश्वरधाममा रहेको प्राकृतिक शिलामाथि अवस्थित स्वयं प्रकट शिवलिङ्ग विशेष आकर्षणको केन्द्र हो । एउटै ९ रोपनी क्षेत्रफलको विशाल चट्टानमाथि रहेको यो शिवलिङ्ग देश–विदेशका भक्तजनका लागि श्रद्धाको केन्द्र बनेको छ ।

विशेषगरी साउन महिना, महाशिवरात्रि, बालाचतुर्दशी तथा तीजका अवसरमा यहाँ हजारौँ श्रद्धालुको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ ।

धेरै धार्मिक स्थलहरुमा पछि स्थापना गरिएको शिवलिङ्गमा पुजा गरिन्छ भने गलेश्वरधाममा स्वयं उत्पत्ती ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग भएको हुँदा पनि यस स्थानको छुट्टै धार्मिक महत्व हुने बताइन्छ ।

साउनको दोस्रो सोमबार भक्तजनले चढाएको भेटी गणना गरी बेनीस्थित गरिमा विकास बैंकमा दाखिला गरिएको छ । पहिलो सोमबार करिब दुई लाख रुपैयाँ भेटी संकलन भएको गलेश्वरधाममा दोस्रो सोमबार पनि करिब सोही हाराहारी रकम संकलन भएको थियो । भक्तजनको संख्या केही घटे पनि धार्मिक आस्थाका साथ दर्शन गर्ने क्रम भने निरन्तर भइरहेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र परिसरमा निर्माण गरिएको १०८ शिवलिङ्ग भक्तजनका लागि अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण बनेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र विकास कोषका उपाध्यक्ष बमबहादुर पुनको अगुवाइमा चन्दा तथा सहयोगबाट संकलित करिब साढे १३ लाख रुपैयाँमध्ये साढे ७ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर शिवलिङ्ग निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

२०७६ सालमा निर्माण गरीएको यो धार्मिक महत्व दिने आकृति एकै स्थानमा १०८ शिवलिङ्गको दर्शन र पूजा गर्न सकिने भएपछि दैनिक रूपमा भक्तजन पुग्ने गरेका छन् ।

धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक र प्राकृतिक सम्पदाको अनुपम संगमका रूपमा रहेको गलेश्वरधामले म्याग्दीको धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धनमा समेत महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ । २०८२ सालका चार वटा सोमबार गरी झण्डै १७ लाख रुपियाँ भेटी संकलन भएको थियो ।

articles.title: Nepal raises dismantling of Susta earthen barrier with New Delhi
articles.summary:
The Nepali Embassy in New Delhi on Sunday formally raised with India’s Ministry of External Affairs an incident in which Indian security personnel crossed into Nepali territory in Susta in Nawalparasi West and dismantled a mud embankment built by local villagers to protect their village from flooding.

The embassy raised the issue on the same day of the incident.

“Our officials raised concerns about the way Indian security personnel dismantled the makeshift embankment,” said a foreign ministry official, adding, “We told them that it was a last-resort effort by locals to mitigate flooding.”

Susta and Kalapani are two major boundary disputes between Nepal and India, with both sides acknowledging them as contested areas. In 2014, both sides agreed that the issue would be resolved through the mechanism involving foreign secretaries and the Boundary Working Group. However, in the past 12 years, no meeting at the foreign secretary level has been held to address the dispute.

According to two officials at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Indian side insisted that Susta and where the Nepali side is building the mud dam are disputed territories and that both sides had agreed to maintain the status quo.

A similar dispute erupted two months ago when India's SSB personnel halted the construction of a permanent flood-control embankment being built by the Nepal government in the same area. Following a minor scuffle at the time, officials from Nepal’s Armed Police Force (AFP) and India’s SSB reached an agreement to maintain the status quo, stating that Susta is a mutually agreed disputed area.

On Sunday also, the Indian side reiterated the same position, calling the area disputed and saying no new structure could be constructed there, according to the two officials.

Besides regular meetings between the security agencies, the chief district officer and district magistrate of the Indian side do sit regularly if any dispute arises along the border.

Dipak Nepal, the chief district officer of Nawalparasi West, told the Post that the situation was normal on Monday.

As soon as Nepali media reported the matter on Sunday, the Nepali Embassy in New Delhi took it up with the Indian side, seeking a prompt resolution. However, the Indian side called for restraint and said the issue should not be turned into a national agenda.

The dispute intensified after Nepal awarded a contract to construct a 132-metre flood-protection embankment along the Narayani River. According to local officials, the project could not proceed after the Indian side raised objections, leaving the entire stretch without permanent protection. They said Nepal has already completed embankment construction downstream of the 132-metre section, while the disputed stretch remains the only unprotected gap.

Since then, the exposed riverbank has continued to suffer severe erosion caused by the Narayani River. Local residents say they attempted to build temporary protective structures to mitigate the immediate risk of flooding, but those efforts were also halted, despite the works being carried out within Nepali territory and outside the disputed section.

Officials and local communities warn that the unprotected stretch has become one of the main entry points for monsoon floodwaters into Susta. They maintain that Nepal’s objective in constructing the embankment is to protect its territory, farmland and settlements from river erosion and flooding. As Indian territory lies both upstream and downstream of this section of the river, some local officials also believe that coordinated embankment and river-training works on both sides would be necessary for effective flood management.

In the absence of protective measures, they say, riverbank erosion continues to reduce the area of Nepali land in Susta year after year.

On Sunday, according to locals, a group of Indian security personnel in plain clothes entered Nepali territory carrying spades and began digging up the mud embankment that villagers had recently built to reduce the risk of floodwaters from the Narayani river inundating the settlement.

Residents rushed to stop them, triggering a standoff before Nepal’s Armed Police Force intervened to prevent the situation from escalating.

Later as per the past agreement, APF and SSB personnel quickly brought the situation under control.

On 8 December 1988 Nepal and India agreed to treat the Narayani River as a boundary river under the principle of a fixed boundary, according to former Director General Buddhi Narayan Shrestha.

Under this principle, the boundary remains fixed as it existed when the Nepal-India boundary agreement was signed, he added.

“Fixed boundary principle applies to the demarcation of the riverine sector of Tarai lowlands. It requires identifying the river’s course as it existed at the time of the agreement and demarcating the boundary by placing alternative pillars on both sides of the river, regardless of whether water or river channel exists there today. This principle was adopted as per the decision of Nepal government on 8 December 1988 and agreed upon by both countries,” said Shrestha.

However, over the last several decades, the Narayani River has changed course, creating complications over land ownership and leading to competing claims in the area.

Rabindra Jaiswal, spokesperson for the Susta Protection Campaign, said villagers had constructed the temporary earthen embankment only after Indian authorities blocked them from building a permanent flood-control structure along the Narayani River.

While 16 border pillars mark most of the Nepal-India boundary in Nawalparasi West, there are no boundary pillars along the roughly 24-kilometre Susta stretch.

Instead, the two countries rely on natural features such as rivers and trees to mark the boundary. As a result disputes over land ownership and cultivation recur frequently. A silk cotton tree currently serves as the de facto boundary marker in part of the disputed area.

Residents say the changing course of the Narayani river over the decades has further complicated the border.

Sunday’s incident followed a similar dispute on May 31, when India’s SSB entered ward 5 of Susta Rural Municipality and objected to the construction of a permanent embankment being built by Nepal’s Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation.

According to Chief District Officer Nepal, the dispute centred on a new 132-metre section of embankment planned about 50 metres to the east of an existing structure, still within Nepali territory.

The project was initiated after then energy minister Kulman Ghising visited Susta about eight months ago and directed authorities to prioritise flood protection for the vulnerable settlement.

Susta is bounded by the Narayani river to the north and west and India’s Bihar state to the south and east.

India maintains three SSB outposts near the area, while Nepal has an APF border post commanded by an inspector.

Residents say Indian authorities have repeatedly objected to Nepal’s activities in the area, citing the absence of clearly demarcated border pillars.

Two weeks ago, 52 residents led by Susta campaigner Munna Khan travelled to Kathmandu and staged a protest at Maitighar Mandala, demanding stronger state protection.

During a meeting with Home Minister Sudan Gurung, they urged the government to establish a Nepali Army security post in Susta, alleging years of harassment by Indian security personnel.

Following the meeting, the home ministry instructed the district administration to reinforce security in sensitive areas of Susta and to begin processing citizenship applications for eligible residents who lack citizenship documents.

articles.title: Anti-snake venom shortage hits hospitals nationwide
articles.summary:
Amid the peak snakebite season, hospitals and snakebite treatment centres across the country are facing critical shortages of anti-snake venom. As a result, hundreds of snakebite victims are at risk of being left without the live-saving antidote.

The failure of the authorities to replenish anti-snake venom stocks has left medics and health facilities struggling to treat critically ill snakebite patients.

“We don’t have a single dose of anti-snake venom and haven’t received any supplies for hospitals and snakebite treatment centres,” Ujjwal Yadav, information officer at the Provincial Health Logistic Management Centre in Madhesh province, told the Post over the phone from Janakpur. “The number of venomous snakebite incidents has risen significantly of late, but we don’t have any anti-snake venom to supply.”

Snakebites and related deaths are common in Nepal during the summer.

At least 53 people died and 716 others have been hospitalised after venomous snakebites since May 14 this year, according to data from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

However, figures from individual snakebite treatment centres suggest the actual number of cases is much higher.

In Kapilvastu, the Gorusinge-based treatment centre alone has treated over 500 snakebite cases since mid-April, including over a dozen involving venomous snakes.

The antidote cannot be purchased from pharmacies, as it is supplied free of charge by the government.

There are 27 snakebite treatment centres in the Madhesh province. Hospitals also provide treatment to the snakebite victims, meaning the centre has to supply the antidote to hospitals also.

“Most snakebite treatment centres in our province have exhausted their stocks,” said Yadav. “Some have only five vials left, others 11. We receive dozens of phone calls from health workers requesting anti-snake venom every day, but we don’t have any.”

Health officials say they have repeatedly asked the federal health ministry to replenish stocks, but to no avail. Madhesh alone needs 800 to 1,000 vials each year.

“The risk of patients dying increases if anti-snake venom is not available,” said Salik Ram Kalathoki, information officer at Rapti Academy of Health Sciences. “In such cases, there is also a greater risk of medics and health facilities being attacked by victims’ relatives.”

Officials say that the academy has run out of anti-snake venom and has asked nearby snakebite treatment centres to provide supplies if critically ill patients need to be referred.

Almost all snakebite treatment centres and health facilities in Lumbini province have run out of anti-snake venom, according to officials at the Provincial Health Logistics Management Centre in the province.

“The responsibility for supplying anti-snake venom to the provinces lies with the federal government,” said Dr Rajendra Kumar Giri, director of the centre. “This year, the [federal] Ministry of Health and Food Safety has not supplied us with the required quantity of anti-snake venom.”

“We even brought some doses from the Karnali provincial government’s agency because their demand is lower than ours,” said Giri.

Meanwhile, officials at the Epidemiology and Disease Control Division said they have supplied 60 vials of anti-snake venom to Lumbini province on Monday.

“We know this is not sufficient, as there are over 40 snakebite treatment centres and hospitals in the province,” an official at the division said, asking not to be named as he is not authorised to speak to the media.

Health workers in the province said that in some cases, a single patient needs more than 20 vials of anti-snake venom, particularly if bitten by a king cobra or a krait.

Officials at the division said it may take over two weeks for fresh supplies to reach treatment centres, even if suppliers deliver within the promised timeframe.

In recent days, venomous snakebites have increasingly been reported from hilly and mountain districts. Experts attribute the spread of snakes beyond the Tarai to rising temperatures driven by climate change. Warmer conditions may be pushing them to the hilly and mountainous districts, where they were previously not found.

Nepal is among the countries vulnerable to the climate crisis and has witnessed multiple extreme weather events over the past decade and a half.

Evidence suggests that maximum temperatures in Nepal are rising at a faster annual rate of 0.056 degrees Celsius, compared to the global average rise of 0.03 degrees Celsius each year.

Compared to the districts of the Tarai region, those in the hills and mountains have been witnessing a more rapid increase in daytime maximum temperatures, which could have helped venomous snakes survive there, according to the experts.

According to a report published in The Lancet, a leading international medical journal, in March 2022, around 2,700 people, mostly children and women from the plains, die from snakebites in Nepal every year.

Experts say many snakebite deaths are preventable and blame the high death toll on shortages of anti-snake venom, a lack of trained physicians, poor health infrastructure, delays in reaching health facilities, lack of intensive care and dialysis services.

The government has committed to halving the deaths and disabilities caused by snakebite envenomation by 2030, a national target aligned with the World Health Organisation’s ‘Snakebite Roadmap’.

articles.title: Players and legends urge action as Nepal risk first-ever absence from SAFF Championship
articles.summary:
There are two countries that have participated in all 14 editions of the SAFF Men’s Championship to date—India and Nepal. That, however, might change this year. As Bangladesh are preparing to host the championship’s 15th edition in November, Nepal could miss playing at the biggest South Asian footballing event for the first time in history.

Nepal’s participation in South Asia’s premier international football tournament hinges on a critical condition: FIFA must lift the current suspension on the All Nepal Football Association before the stipulated SAFF deadline on September 30.

If that doesn’t happen, the beleaguered Nepali football would face another blow. Nepal have already missed out on five major football events this year.

Amid this, stakeholders have started pressuring the government—through social media—to help lift the FIFA suspension at the earliest.

“Honourable Prime Minister, today, the future of thousands of Nepali football players stands in jeopardy,” Hari Khadka, ANFA’s technical director, wrote on his Facebook on Sunday afternoon. “If a timely solution is not found, Nepal faces the grim reality of missing out on the upcoming SAFF Football Championship as well.”

Khadka, who is Nepal’s all-time joint highest goal scorer, added, “To safeguard years of hard work, dreams, and national pride of our athletes, I respectfully request you to consult with the concerned stakeholders, take the necessary initiatives, and foster an environment where Nepali players can step onto the pitch once again.”

The South Asian Football Federation has shown extreme flexibility towards Nepal. “In the event that Nepal’s FIFA suspension is lifted by September 30, Nepal will be included in the group of the hosts Bangladesh,” SAFF announced during the draw ceremony for the SAFF Championship in Thimpu, Bhutan, on Saturday.

Bangladesh were drawn into Group A alongside Sri Lanka and Bhutan, while Group B comprises India, Pakistan and the Maldives.

But Nepal needs the FIFA suspension, which was imposed on June 24 citing continuous third-party interference, to be lifted. And it is only possible when the incumbent ANFA President Pankaj Bikram Nembang’s plan for an early election is allowed to resume from the point it was stopped in Jhapa on March 26 after the government’s intervention.

Nembang is allowed to host an early election, and it abides by FIFA and ANFA Statutes, the governing body of international football has stated multiple times. However, the National Sports Council (NSC) has had a separate opinion that ANFA can conduct its elections only after ensuring a fresh mandate at the district associations.

“It is not a fair election if there are the same voters, who helped Nembang win the previous election, at the district level,” the NSC has been stressing.

Despite Nembang’s four-year term ending only in mid-June, he had put forth the plan to organise it as early as February. “We cannot force district associations to conduct their elections before time because they are independent bodies,” Kiran Rai, ANFA general secretary, has been defending Nembang’s move.

With the two authorities—ANFA and NSC—at loggerheads, the NSC even had ANFA suspended for up to three months on March 25, two days before ANFA’s election in Jhapa. It was later lifted following warnings of suspension from FIFA, but ANFA was still under state scrutiny.

It was only after the government disallowed ANFA representatives from flying abroad to participate in FIFA’s Congress, Summit and World Cup that the international footballing body had enough and imposed the suspension.

FIFA’s suspension means that Nepali football cannot exercise any of its membership rights. “Other member associations may not entertain sporting contact with a suspended member association,” FIFA stated in a circular to all of its members.

As a result, Nepal could not participate in the AFC Women’s Champions League 2026/27, AFC U17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers and AFC U20 Asian Cup Qualifiers.

Had Nepal’s suspension been lifted by August 1, Nepal, who were drawn in Group I alongside Mongolia, Guam and Northern Mariana Islands on May 28, could have had the opportunity to play in the U20 Qualifiers. Now, the fixtures are out, and Nepal are not listed in the group.

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC), on June 27, had written a letter to ANFA stating that the deadlines to lift the FIFA suspension in order to ensure participation at the Women’s Champions League and U17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers were on June 29 and July 13, respectively. As the suspension continued, Nepal were excluded.

However, Nepal had lost two other footballing events, long before the FIFA suspension, to the tussle between ANFA and NSC.

Firstly, a friendly between the men’s teams of Nepal and Hong Kong scheduled for March 26 was cancelled after the NSC, as per ANFA, did not allow the use of Dasharath Stadium. The NSC, meanwhile, defended itself by making public permission letters provided to ANFA.

Secondly, Nepal women’s team could not travel to Thailand in mid-April for the FIFA Series as ANFA withdrew from the tournament citing NSC’s suspension. The women’s team were training in a closed camp for the Series when they heard the bad news.

As they were denied participation in the FIFA Series, the women’s team could not train properly during the closed camp for the SAFF Women’s Championship, which Nepal played in Goa, India, from May 25.

“There were noises of FIFA suspension when the team was training. As they had missed the FIFA Series already, they were in continuous fear of missing the SAFF tournament as well,” Nabin Neupane, the team’s head coach, had told the Post earlier. “They were not focused on training. How could they even?”

Neupane also took to social media on Sunday and requested the government to take necessary steps to ensure the men’s team did not lose the opportunity.

“Honourable Prime Minister, the SAFF Championship is like the World Cup to us. It is not merely a tournament—it is an opportunity tied to the dreams, hard work, and futures of thousands of Nepali players and coaches,” Neupane, who is also a former national player, wrote. “Considering the future of Nepali footballers, please create a suitable environment to play.”

Similarly, Nepal’s captain Kiran Chemjong posted a photo of the teams divided into two groups for the SAFF Championship on his Facebook story. He then wrote, “As a proud Nepali footballer, seeing Nepal’s name missing from the upcoming SAFF schedule is heartbreaking.”

He added, “We have always fought for our country with pride, passion and hope,” Chemjong continued. “We sincerely hope that the ban will be lifted soon and that Nepal will once again be on the pitch, representing our nation and making our people proud.”

Manish Dangi, another national player, had also requested the same from the state.

The Post has been trying to reach out to Minister for Education and Sports Sasmit Pokharel and the ministry’s spokesperson Shiva Kumar Sapkota for comments for weeks. However, they have not responded despite repetitive calls and messages.

Minister Pokharel had publicly stated a couple of weeks ago that the government was in communication with FIFA and AFC and had called their representatives for dialogue. He has not spoken about the issue since then.

The Post has also sought a response from FIFA on the matter through the formal channel for media.

articles.title: Inside Kaptanganj: How a religious flag dispute and a loudspeaker turned a border village deadly
articles.summary:
Om Prakash Mehta was already in bed at around 9 pm on the evening of July 26. But as tensions began rising at the Kaptanganj Chowk, about 700 metres from his home, he watched videos on social media of his own friends at the scene, and decided to go there as well. His father, Krishnadev, tried to stop him, but he didn’t listen.

At around 10 pm, Krishnadev called his 31-year-old son and asked him to come back quickly. “I’ll be there soon,” Om Prakash said, before ending the call. Right then, gunfire erupted at the chowk. Moments later, Krishnadev received a call from one of his son’s friends. “Om Prakash has been shot,” he was told.

By the time Krishnadev ran and arrived at the chowk, Om Prakash had already been placed in an ambulance and taken to the Neuro Hospital in Biratnagar. People there told him it wasn’t very serious and that he’d recover.

Krishnadev changed his clothes and arrived at the hospital, about 25 kilometres east. By then, Om Prakash had been placed on a ventilator. Next morning, his relatives and neighbours told him that the treatment was going well, and he should go home and take care of his wife.

While Krishnadev was returning to Kaptanganj, news of Om Prakash’s death began to spread on social media. His nephew, who was driving, broke the news on their way back.

“As soon as I heard it, I lost consciousness,” Krishnadev recalled. The last time he saw Om Prakash was when he’d left his bed that night, ignoring his plea to stay back.

On the other side of the settlement, west of Om Prakash’s house and about 100 metres south of Kaptanganj Chowk, lives 72-year-old Mohammad Tahir Miyan.

On the afternoon of July 27, a day after tensions began in town, a curfew had already been imposed in Kaptanganj. At around noon, an angry crowd of young men with bottles filled with petrol arrived at Tahir’s house. “They began sprinkling petrol and set the house on fire,” he said.Those inside the house managed to escape, but two houses — belonging to his eldest and third sons — and a pile of straw were burned down.

“We had always lived like brothers,” Tahir said, struggling to come to terms with what had just happened over the last 24 hours. Kaptanganj, located in Dewanganj Rural Municipality about one kilometre south of the Indian border, had no history of Hindu-Muslim violence. Om Prakash was killed in police firing. Tahir’s house was destroyed by an enraged mob. The shared account of these two families from two different communities — Hindu and Muslim — is simple: “Nothing like this had ever happened here.”

The dispute that began there eventually claimed three lives. Jay Prakash Mehta, 21, who was also from Kaptanganj, died four days later while undergoing treatment for a gunshot injury. Ganesh Yadav, 15, from Golbazar of Siraha, also died on July 30. Bystanders say he died in police firing. However, in an interview with Kantipur, Home Minister Sudan Gurung denied that the police shot Yadav.

Kantipur’s field reporting, interviews with more than a dozen people, and a review of previous records suggest that the violence in Kaptanganj unfolded amid a wider pattern of simmering religious tensions in some parts of the Madhesh. In recent years, local disputes, social media amplification, political mobilisation, and repeated institutional failures have been contributing to escalation. This time, it had turned deadly.

The Armed Police Force, Nepal’s border security and riot control force, had flagged the risk of growing communal violence some three years ago, especially in the Madhesh region. A senior APF official familiar with the report told Kantipur last week that the force had repeatedly briefed the political leadership on the risks posed by rising communal polarisation, but its recommendations were largely ignored.

The episode also highlights failures at multiple levels — local authorities that neglected early warning signs, security agencies that responded after violence had already broken out, and political actors who largely remained on the sidelines until there were casualties from the conflict.

Kathmandu, however, largely remained passive in the face of violence that broke out in Kaptanganj, with its immediate response limited to reshuffling of police and administrative officials. Curfew came into effect at 7 am on July 27.

In the days that followed, protests spread throughout Sunsari, then to Morang and later to Siraha, Saptari and Dhanusha. Security personnel were deployed in large numbers as local authorities imposed curfews, yet protesters defied the restrictions. As calls grew for Prime Minister Balendra Shah to address the nation and for Home Minister Gurung to visit the incident site, both leaders faced criticism for their response. Neither appeared in Parliament; Shah instead expressed grief over the deadly clashes on social media while Gurung remained in Kathmandu. Shah also skipped an all-party meeting called by his party chair Rabi Lamichhane to discuss the spread of violence across Madhesh.

Dewanganj Rural Municipality, one of the 12 local levels in Sunsari district, lies about 25 kilometres south of the district headquarters, Inaruwa. According to the 2021 census, the municipality has a population of fewer than 40,000, with Hindus making up 86 percent and Muslims 14 percent. This Maithili- and Magahi-speaking region is largely dependent on agriculture. Nearly two-thirds of households use firewood or cow dung cakes for cooking, while only one in 10 households uses LPG gas. Many young people have migrated to Gulf countries or Malaysia, leaving villages with a larger presence of elderly people, women, and teenagers.

The people who appeared on the streets after the night of July 26 were mostly teenagers and young who had only recently entered adulthood. Elderly and responsible members of both communities remain bewildered with what happened.

“How did something like this suddenly happen?” That is the question many are asking as things try to return to normal after a week.

The dispute that eventually erupted into violence last Sunday began about a month earlier. On June 28, the Muslim community celebrated Muharram on public land at Naya Hatiya Bazaar in Kaptanganj after receiving permission from the ward office.

“We have been observing Muharram for 50 years,” said 36-year-old Jabir Alam, a goat and sheep trader. “Earlier there was a Shiva temple here. Now a Kali temple has been built, one temple after another. We do not have a fixed place, and we have celebrated wherever the local government gives us permission.”

On the day of Muharram, the Muslim community planted 40–50 religious flags at the public site, along with Nepal’s national flag. After the festival ended, two religious flags and the national flag remained there, according to Jabir, for another gathering scheduled after 40 days. They removed the rest themselves.

Before the next gathering after 40 days, Shrawan had begun — the month when Hindu devotees worship Shiva, undertake Bol Bam pilgrimages, and visit temples in large numbers. Hindu residents requested the ward office to take initiative to remove the flags placed near the Shiva temple.

“About ten days earlier, after there was a dispute over the flags, I myself went and said — if the flags are causing problems, we will remove them; let’s not create a dispute,” Jabir said. “But the ward chairman and rural municipality chairman did not pay any attention.”

Shatrughan Prasad Mehta, former principal of the local Babuji Basic School, also points to the same failure by local authorities.

“The ward chairman gave land for celebrating Muharram,” he said. “But afterwards, when our boys asked him not to leave the flags there, he paid no heed to the request.”

On July 26, according to Manoj Kumar Pokharel, the local coordinator for human rights organisation INSEC, a group of youth removed the flags that had been placed there earlier and replaced them with new flags bearing images of Hanuman.

That night, Hindu youths preparing for the Bol Bam pilgrimage the following day, gathered near the Shiva temple. They were playing songs on loudspeakers, including “Jai Shri Ram” and “Bol Bam ka Nara Hai, Baba Ek Sahara Hai.”

They planned to travel about 40 kilometres northwest to the Koshi Barrage to collect holy water and return to offer it at the Shiva temple. The loudspeaker installed on a vehicle facing north was turned toward the south, where the Muslim settlement begins about 100 metres away.

According to people from the Hindu community, Muslim youths went there to object to the playing of those songs. People from the Muslim community, however, claim that the songs were played on loudspeakers at a very high volume toward the Muslim settlement located south of the Shiva temple, and that 8 to10 motorcycles with Indian number plates were repeatedly riding through the road, creating fear among them.

Soon, tensions escalated, a verbal confrontation began, followed by a physical clash. There is no single account of what happened next.

People from the Hindu community say that Muslim youths, who had come in greater numbers than the Hindu youths, started beating them and when they got beaten back, the Muslim youths themselves informed the police. Members of the Muslim community say they did not beat anyone but informed the police after sensing that the dispute could escalate.

Based on details gathered through their field investigation, INSEC’s Pokharel said that the boys from the Hindu side were fewer in number. “Initially, they were beaten,” he said. “Then some among them exaggerated the incident and sought support from the village.”

By then, the police had arrived. “After the police told them to leave, the Muslim youths went home. But the Hindu youths refused to return, saying they had been beaten and wanted revenge,” Pokharel said. “They tried to move toward the Muslim settlement, and then there was a clash with the police who tried to stop them.”

Jabir’s account is broadly consistent with Pokharel’s version.

“The police stopped us in our own neighbourhood, and after that we did not go anywhere. The police stopped them from coming here from the north. During the pushing and shoving, they clashed with the police,” he said. “There was no Hindu-Muslim fight. There was a clash between them and the police. Not a single person from the Muslim side was injured. There are only 50–60 Muslim households here, while they are in the hundreds. How can we survive by fighting them here?”

Although an incident like the one in Kaptanganj had not been seen before, a review of records from previous years shows that the surrounding region has had some history of tensions linked to religious disputes.

According to INSEC records, seven such incidents have been recorded in Sunsari alone — three in 2024, two in 2025, and two so far in 2026. Publicly available reports show that such incidents have occurred from Sunsari westward through Madhesh districts all the way to Nepalgunj.

Kantipur found records of at least 17 such incidents in the Terai over an eight-year period, from 2018/19 until now. Since this list is based only on incidents reported in the media, it represents the minimum number. These incidents occurred in districts ranging from Banke in the west, to Parsa in the centre, and Sunsari in the east. All of these are Terai-Madhesh districts bordering India.

The causes of these incidents also appear to be similar. Around two-thirds of the 17 incidents (11 cases) involved disputes during religious processions and idol immersions held during festivals: immersions related to Durga, Lakshmi, Saraswati and Krishna Janmashtami; processions for Ram Navami and Hanuman Jayanti; Chhath and Kalash processions. In many of these cases, the administration had to impose curfews.

In recent years, social media has become a powerful channel through which local disputes are rapidly amplified and spread. Whether it was an insensitive Facebook post by a Hindu youth in Nepalgunj or an offensive comment against Hinduism by a Muslim youth in Rajbiraj — neither of which Kantipur is linking to or describing in detail — anger that often begins online has started spilling onto the streets.

Chandrakishore, a journalist and author who regularly writes about the Madhesh, believes that the growing access to social media has helped spread tensions rapidly.

“The person who was killed in Kaptanganj had gone to bed. After an allegation or rumour reached him through social media, he came running outside,” he said. “These days videos appear immediately on social media. YouTubers livestream everything, and there is no time for filtering good and bad or right and wrong.”

Incidents deliberately aimed at insulting and provoking another community have also become public. Last year, near the election period in Birgunj, police arrested three people carrying a pig’s head and homemade bombs allegedly intended to be thrown inside a mosque. In Gaur, a dispute occurred after loudspeakers were used during a Hindu wedding procession while prayers were being conducted.

Muslims are Nepal’s third-largest religious group. According to the 2021 census, Muslims make up 5.1 percent of the population. Most of them live in the Terai districts.

The United States Department of State’s 2023 report on religious freedom included complaints from Muslim leaders advocating religious inclusion that they faced pressure from both government officials and the Hindu community.

Dinesh Shrestha, chairman of the Biratnagar chapter of North-South Collectives, a Madhesh-based think-tank, says such disputes that have recently become public are not isolated incidents occurring suddenly or by chance.

“There appears to be an organised effort to increase religious conflict in Nepal,” he said, without identifying those whom he believed were responsible for fomenting such conflicts. “Whether it is incidents that happened elsewhere in the past or the current Kaptanganj incident — all of these have happened as part of that effort.”

Jayaprakash Prasad Gupta, a former minister and the author of the book “Madhesh: Saamajik Samrachana ra Bibhed,” points to the influence from across the border in India.

“In the past, Bihar had governments shaped by caste structures. Now there is BJP’s Hindu-majoritarian politics,” he said. “Nepal too has been becoming polarised under its direct influence.”

Chandrakishore says that four trends seen in growing religious tensions in recent years are reflected in the Kaptanganj incident.

The first trend is the positioning taken by members of the same community elsewhere when an incident occurs in one place. “If something ordinary happens in Malangwa, immediately a procession comes out in Bhairahawa. Earlier, such matters would end locally; they did not spread elsewhere,” he said.

The second trend is the unspoken competition seen in public religious activities in recent years. “If one person puts up one microphone, I have to put up four; if he breaks two swords, I have to break four; if he drives 25 motorcycles, I have to drive 50,” he said.

The third trend, he says, is going in front of another community’s place of worship and loudly raising one’s own community’s slogans as a direct challenge.

The fourth trend is how these conflicts are addressed. Earlier, political representatives played the central role in meetings aimed at reducing social tensions. That space, he says, has been replaced by representatives claiming to speak on the basis of religious identity.

“Suddenly, someone emerged as a Muslim leader, while someone else began attending meetings as a Hindu leader,” he said. “If they had remained in political parties, they might have been ordinary party workers. But now they have become leaders.”

Ram Rijan Yadav, who used to be active in the Janata Samajbadi Party, led by Upendra Yadav, says he has personally witnessed how religious politics from across the border has begun influencing Madhesh. Four years ago, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had already built an organisation inside their party. “The ‘Yadav boys’ who were part of our party committees had already become associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS),” he said.

That growing religious polarisation is also visible in the symbols that have appeared across the public landscape.

At Kaptanganj Chowk and along the route west through Biratnagar, Itahari, Inaruwa and into Madhesh, the same image appears repeatedly — on flags, at intersections, outside shops, on rooftops and electricity poles.

The image is of Hanuman. But it is not the traditional depiction of the deity; it is an angry-looking version of Hanuman. The high-contrast image, featuring saffron and black colours and a tightened face, also appears as stickers placed on motorcycles and vehicles.

“The Hanuman I saw while growing up was peaceful,” said Yadav. “For the last two or four years, I have started seeing images of a very angry Hanuman everywhere in Madhesh. The Bajrang Dal and Hindu nationalist groups have promoted this image,” Yadav said.

The image is not rooted in Nepal’s traditional religious iconography. According to reports in Indian media, the ‘angry Hanuman’ image was created in 2015 by Kerala-based graphic designer Karan Acharya. Reports say Acharya designed it for a local temple’s Ganesh Chaturthi festival after friends asked him to create a Hanuman with “a different expression.”

The saffron-and-black image soon became popular across India and later appeared in Nepal as well.

“Culturally and religiously, Hanuman’s image is peaceful. What we have learned is that Hanuman represents knowledge, virtues and humility,” Chandrakishore said. “But for political purposes, Hanumanji was made to appear angry.”

Five days after violence began, the situation in Madhesh began gradually returning to normal following Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s address to the nation, RSP leader Rabi Lamichhane’s marathon meetings, the Home Minister’s field visit, agreements with affected families, appeals by political parties for harmony, and continued dialogue among representatives of different communities at the local level.

But civil society activists warn that if rising religious suspicion among communities is not addressed, the tension may only appear to have subsided while remaining alive beneath the surface, waiting to flare up again.

Curfew has now been lifted in Kaptanganj. Army armoured vehicles stationed at intersections have been withdrawn. Yet, a sense of unease continues to linger over the village.

Both Om Prakash and Jay Prakash had left their homes after learning that tensions had intensified at Naya Hatiya. According to eyewitness Ramesh Kumar Mehta, the crowd became even more agitated after Om Prakash collapsed after being shot by the police.

“People were running in different directions. At that moment, Jay Prakash was also shot in the courtyard of the Shiva temple,” Ramesh said.

In the courtyard of a small hut about 500 metres north of Naya Hatiya, Jay Prakash’s auto-rickshaw has remained parked since the day of the incident.

In Om Prakash’s father’s room, the fan has remained still since Krishnadev left that night after his son was shot.

Tahir Miyan no longer has a house.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s secular fabric is facing its toughest test yet
articles.summary:
The recent unrest in Tarai-Madhesh, triggered by a communal clash in Devanganj, Sunsari, on July 26, has reminded Nepal of its vulnerability to religious friction. The Nepali state has historically relied upon coercive force to maintain fragile peace. Such reactive measures are insufficient to address the undercurrents currently threatening the nation’s social fabric. It is now a matter of national urgency that the government initiates a rigorous and transparent investigation into the burgeoning influence and tactical operations of extremist religious outfits whose activities are increasingly linked to the propagation of religious hate in Nepal.

Nepal’s modern political identity was built upon a foundation of secular mobilisation, which has long existed in a state of tension with a historically Hinduised state structure. This friction has been exacerbated over the last decade, as political actors began instrumentalising religion for mobilisation. The rise of a religion-centric power structure in neighbouring states has further catalysed the shift in Nepal, empowering the religious organisations to mobilise resources across the border and expand their networks.

The methodology of this expansion warrants intense scrutiny. Alarmingly, current trends indicate the adoption of fluid organisational structures as a deliberate strategy to evade accountability. Rather than operating through identifiable entities, various groups are rapidly formed under innocuous banners only to be dissolved or rebranded once their immediate objectives of spreading religious rhetoric are achieved. This tactic, likely imported from contemporary practices in neighbouring states, makes it nearly impossible for journalists, researchers, or auditors to track funding sources and institutional affiliations. The state, therefore, seems to be the only mechanism capable of tracing the external influence on such organisations.

The reported involvement of retired high-ranking security officials, including former generals, with these religious-political organisations is another concern for national security. The recruitment of such individuals provides radical networks with tactical knowledge required to manipulate community-level violence. Meanwhile, the security apparatus remains characterised by an institutionalised insensitivity and a command mentality that prioritises punishment over dialogue. When the state relies on the indiscriminate use of force, coupled with former high-level security officials joining radical networks, it enables radical networks to use violence to rattle the social fabric.

The current administration’s failure to address the underlying causes of communal triggers is no longer tenable. The state’s historical amnesia regarding the roots of communal violence allows radical groups like the Hindu Samrat Sena to benefit from a fragmented landscape while maintaining links to extremist ideologies.

A meaningful response to this crisis requires more than traditional nationalist rhetoric, temporary curfews, or solidarity rallies. The authorities must empower the civil society of regional hubs, such as Biratnagar and Janakpur, to conduct autonomous investigations into communal incidents rather than waiting for orders from a centralised and often distracted leadership in Kathmandu. There must also be a concerted effort to foster an informed and critical citizenship capable of engaging in dialogue before tensions spiral into violence. Concurrently, the security forces need to be trained extensively in conflict de-escalation.

The preservation of Nepal’s secular identity demands that the state confront the opaque funding and fluid tactics of the organisations linked to extremist religious outfits. Failure to investigate these networks will only signal to the public—and to the international community—that the rule of law has been surrendered to the interests of imported religious radicalism.

articles.title: Nepal’s problematic foreign policy: Symbols without substance
articles.summary:
The greatest problem among Nepali politicians is that they lose the opportunity at hand and indulge in blame games to hide their failures. This has happened since the dawn of democracy in 1951 and continues to this day. Most of the time, opportunities were squandered due to a lack of direction and attempts to falsify politics by pointing fingers at a foreign hand, making foreign policy a mobilising strategy to score domestic political gains, particularly at a time when the regime faced a survival crisis. In the post-1960 decades, the consolidation of power for individual aggrandisement and ambition sidetracked the development agenda.

Mixing unclarified concepts with the actual practice of foreign policy has not only obfuscated the issues but also misdirected the executioners. Many such concepts might have symbolic value, but symbols without substance hardly make any progress. Concepts such as the policy of equidistance might be theoretically correct, but they carry no meaning when applied to Nepal’s relations with China and India.

The veritable Nepal-India relations cannot be equated with China, as mainland China is still a distant neighbour despite making Tibet its integral part. Facing south of the Himalayas, and sharing geographical, economic, cultural and humanitarian commonalities, Nepal continues to rely on India in many respects. Thus, even while asserting Nepal’s nationalism and independence, the Nepali power elites have not attempted to dilute the structural relations defined by history as well as by the doctrine of necessity.
